podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Case Remains Open with LAPD
podcast.body: The case of Elliot Smith's death continues to be classified as open by the LAPD, reflecting the lingering uncertainties and the lack of a definitive conclusion regarding the circumstances of his passing. "Today, the case remains open with the LAPD."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Two Stab Wounds
podcast.body: Elliot Smith died on October 21, 2003, at the age of 34, from two stab wounds to the chest. The incident occurred during an argument with his girlfriend, Jennifer, where he reportedly threatened suicide. Jennifer found him with a kitchen knife sticking out of his chest, pulled it out, and called 911, but he later died in the hospital. "Smith died on October 21, 2003. There were two stab wounds in his chest, even fighting with his girlfriend, Jennifer, during which time he threatened to commit suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influential Indie Artist of the 1990s
podcast.body: Elliot Smith, despite not selling a large volume of records, remains deeply loved by his fans and is considered one of the most influential indie artists of the 1990s. His unique style left a lasting impact on the music scene. "Elliot Smith never sold a lot of records, but he remains deeply, deeply loved by his fans. And he's also considered to be one of the most influential indie artists of the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Mortem Praise
podcast.body: Elliot Smith is mentioned as an artist who received praise, alongside Nick Drake and Jeff Buckley, implying a similar post-mortem recognition or heightened appreciation. "Potser Mous Praise for Nick Drake, Jeff Buckley, and Elliot Smith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Songs About David Berkowitz
podcast.body: Elliot Smith is mentioned as one of the artists who have written songs about David Berkowitz, the Son of Sam killer. "They come from everyone from the Beastie Boys to Elliot Smith to Lana Del Rey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Suspicion of Murder Despite Suicide Note
podcast.body: Despite a suicide note and a history of ADHD, depression, suicidal ideation, drug use, and heavy drinking, police, the coroner, and fans remained suspicious of Elliot Smith's death. The primary reason for this suspicion was the absence of "hesitation wounds," as he had stabbed himself cleanly twice directly in the heart. "Police were still suspicious. The corner was suspicious and fans remain suspicious. Why? Mainly because there were no hesitation wounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unusual Nature of Stab Wounds
podcast.body: The method of Elliot Smith's death, two clean stabs directly to the heart without hesitation, is highly unusual for suicide. Statistics indicate that only 4% of suicides involve sharp force trauma, predominantly wrist-slashing. The act of turning a knife sideways and plunging it between the ribs twice without hesitation is considered an extremely painful way to die, fueling theories among fans that "bad drug buddies" might have been involved. "According to statistics on suicide, only 4% of people take their own lives with sharp force trauma and almost all of those involve wrist-slashing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
